body:
Jordan (Support): Escalation from a customer on Dedicated. Started after last night's canary. They report function-calling failures: 25-35% 400s with "schema validation failed" and also cases where the model selected the wrong tool. Filing here to triage.

Maya (Oncall): Can you paste a redacted example of the request + failing response? Also which model/version was rolled?

Jordan (Support): Paste from their report (sensitive fields removed):

```json
POST /v1/chat/completions
{
  "model": "rw-model-neo-1.5",
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"fetch account"}],
  "functions": [
    {"name":"get_account","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"account_id":{"type":"integer"}}}},
    {"name":"list_accounts","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{}}}
  ],
  "function_call":"auto"
}
```

Failing response: 
```json
HTTP/1.1 400
{
  "error": "schema validation failed: functions[0].call.args.account_id expected integer got string"
}
```

Jordan (Support): Customer says they send account_id as a string in some older clients (e.g. "12345"). Previously the runtime coerced basic primitives; appears 1.5 is stricter and the model is returning string args for some calls. Also noticed some calls choose list_accounts instead of get_account for ambiguous prompts.

Sam (ML Eng): Confirmed in canary logs: rw-model-neo-1.5 shows increased policy entropy for function selection and a stricter formatter for function args. Two orthogonal regressions: tool-selection drift, and arg-serialization changes (strings not coerced). We've got counts: function_call 4xx rate for 1.5 = 3.8% vs 0.6% for 1.4 on same test traffic.

Emily (Product): How big is the canary? Which customers hit it? We need to know blast radius and pick mitigation.

Jordan (Support): This customer was in the 15% canary slice. They are on a paid Dedicated plan. Several other smaller orgs reported intermittent errors but only this one hit the 400s consistently.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy rw-model-neo-1.5 -> 15% at 2026-03-14T23:10:12Z

Maya (Oncall): Immediate steps: (1) reduce customer impact, (2) preserve telemetry to debug. Joel, can we pin this org back to 1.4?

Joel (Infra): Yes, can add a per-org override in the router. Will apply override to route org:acct-789 -> rw-model-neo-1.4 and propagate. ETA 3m.

Sam (ML Eng): Meanwhile I'll run a quick repro harness against 1.4/1.5 with varied client payloads (ints as strings, missing fields, extra fields) to characterize. If we can fix in runtime with a compatibility layer (coerce primitive types before validation) we might avoid full rollback. Prototype shim idea: pre-validate hook that coerces number-like strings to numbers per schema. Simple example: 

```js
function coerce(schema, args) {
  for (const [k,v] of Object.entries(schema.properties || {})) {
    if (v.type === 'integer' && typeof args[k] === 'string') {
      const n = parseInt(args[k], 10);
      if (!Number.isNaN(n)) args[k] = n;
    }
  }
  return args;
}
```

Jordan (Support): Customer asked if this is a billing issue too; they saw some errors and duplicate retries. Are they being charged for failed requests?

Emily (Product): Billing policy: we don't charge for server-side validation 400s in most cases. Support confirm and offer to review invoice if they see anomalies. Jordan, reassure customer and log for billing review.

Maya (Oncall): Joel, confirm override applied and that routing metrics show this org on 1.4. Also capture raw logs for a few failed requests before cutover.

Joel (Infra): Override applied at 1719371175. Logs captured from 1719371000-1719371175 and archived to incident bucket. Routing check: now 100% traffic for acct-789 on rw-model-neo-1.4.

Jordan (Support): Customer reports errors stopped after override. They want a timeline for permanent fix and assurance it won't recur.

Sam (ML Eng): Action plan: (A) short term runtime shim + deploy to accept primitive coercions (PR in ~2h), (B) model team to adjust selection priors and serialization behavior for next model patch, (C) add canary validation tests for function-calling (include string-int variations), (D) surface per-model function_call_error_rate in observability.

Emily (Product): Given this affected a paying customer, I'm initiating rollback of the canary to 0% while we validate fixes. We're not rolling back the model code, just pulling the canary percentage.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback rw-model-neo-1.5 -> 0% at 2026-03-15T00:05:00Z by @Emily (Product)

Maya (Oncall): Incident created: INC-2026-03-15-functioncall-regression. Assigning to Sam (ML Eng) and Joel (Infra) for follow-up. Sam please include test matrix and ETA for shim or model patch.

Sam (ML Eng): Will open PR for coercion shim + unit tests (strings-as-ints, floats, nulls). If runtime shim is safe we'll ship as hotfix and re-run canary behind stricter function-calling checks. If not safe, we'll coordinate a model patch. ETA initial PR 2h, QA 6h.

Joel (Infra): I'll add a console shortcut to apply per-org routing overrides and a playbook note for support to request it during regressions. Also will ensure archives include the request/response pairs for debugging.

Jordan (Support): I'll notify the customer we've rolled the canary back and applied routing override. I'll also offer bill review for retries.

Emily (Product): Postmortem items: add function-calling compatibility tests to rollout checklist, require targeted canary customers to opt-in for breaking serializer changes, and add an automated alert for sudden spikes in function_call 4xx by model version.

Sam (ML Eng): Noted. Will include canary unit tests that replay a corpus of historic function calls (including older clients) to validate.

Jordan (Support): Customer is satisfied with rollback + override for now. Keeping incident open until PR and canary tests are green. Closing the immediate escalation.

Maya (Oncall): Oncall resolved. Keeping incident open for postmortem.
